items.title: 56800_John Simmons oral history interview
items.q: So later years, there was three of them: Billy Strayhorn, Jimmy Blanton and Ben. They went out together.

ctx.x: Now, Blanton didn't drink heavily, you know. He'd sip a cocktail now and then. He was very, very -- well, I would say he was a pretty man. He had Indian in him. He had straight hair, high cheekbones, oh, he was something else, really. Dressed beautifully. Had good taste. Dutch boy collars and things like that. Something that you'd never think of wearing, you know? He'd never meet himself twice, you can believe that. Like women wearing dresses?

And I got to Chicago, and this fellow, Tiny Parham, he was a huge man. And he played organ in the Savoy Ballroom. For the skaters, and pre-prize fights, you know, like organists play for ball games and things like that? He was the house band. He played the organ there all the time. However, he would call in for dances. So he called me and asked me, he said, "I understand you're new in the city." I said, "Yes." He says, "Would you like to have a job this weekend?" I said, "Yes." So I went to the job, expecting to…
